narration.text: A licensed Georgia resident may request removal of up to seven points once every five years under the handbook's points-reduction program. A licensed Georgia resident may request removal of up to seven points once every five years under the handbook's points-reduction program. The points-reduction request requires successful completion of a certified six-hour driver-improvement course and the original completion certificate submitted to DDS in person or by mail. The separate points-avoidance process uses a certified six-hour improvement course completed after the citation and before the court appearance, or as the court orders.

why_how.text: Another listed safety-responsibility response is a general or conditional release signed by the claimant and filed with DDS.

The handbook also permits qualifying security for the claimed damages together with the required financial-responsibility filing; DDS holds security for a year and then until the required proof concerning a lawsuit is provided.
A person receiving the safety-responsibility suspension order may request a hearing within ten days of receiving it.

An eligible limited permit restricts driving to approved purposes such as work, scheduled medical care or prescriptions, education, treatment meetings, court or probation duties, community service and specified trips for unlicensed immediate family.
DDS may further limit a permit by destinations, routes, times or vehicle. A limited permit does not authorize commercial-vehicle operation.
A conviction for a moving violation or violation of the permit's own restrictions results in revocation of the limited permit; the handbook also describes extending the underlying suspension.
Eligibility for a limited driving permit depends on the applicable offense, age and conviction record. DDS makes the final eligibility decision; the handbook's examples do not guarantee a permit.
